name: Agnikul Agnibaan

header.one_liner: Agnibaan is Agnikul Cosmos's modular small launcher; its SOrTeD demonstrator flew the world's first flight powered by a single-piece 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine in May 2024.
header.indigenous_label: India-developed at IIT Madras; no audited indigenous percentage disclosed
header.mobility_or_class: Modular small-lift launch vehicle (configurable up to ~300 kg to LEO)

at_a_glance.Launch_site: Agnikul's 'Dhanush' private launchpad, SDSC SHAR, Sriharikota
at_a_glance.Design_payload: Up to ~300 kg to ~700 km LEO (configurable/modular)
at_a_glance.Status: Suborbital demo flown; orbital vehicle in development

what_it_is.prose: Agnibaan is a customisable two-stage small launch vehicle developed by Agnikul Cosmos, a Chennai-based startup incubated at IIT Madras. Its distinguishing technology is the Agnilet engine — a single-piece, fully 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine burning liquid oxygen and aviation-grade kerosene — and a 'plug-and-play' architecture in which the first stage can be configured with a variable number of engines to match a given payload. The design targets up to roughly 300 kg to a 700 km low Earth orbit. On 30 May 2024 Agnikul flew Agnibaan SOrTeD (Suborbital Technology Demonstrator) from its own privately built 'Dhanush' launchpad at Sriharikota — the first flight anywhere powered by a single-piece 3D-printed engine, and India's second private rocket launch; the short flight validated the engine, avionics and the private launch complex before a Bay of Bengal splashdown. ISRO publicly hailed the flight as a milestone. Agnikul manufactures engines in a matter of days rather than weeks, and the SOrTeD flight is the technology base for its planned orbital Agnibaan. This dossier records the demonstrated suborbital milestone and keeps orbital dates and payload economics open.

deployments_procurement.summary: Agnibaan is a commercial launcher in development; its flight activity to date is Agnikul's own suborbital technology demonstration from a private launchpad, not a government procurement.

faq.question: What was the May 2024 milestone?
faq.answer: Agnikul flew Agnibaan SOrTeD, the first rocket flight powered by a single-piece 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine, from its own private launchpad at Sriharikota.

faq.question: What makes Agnibaan unusual?
faq.answer: It is modular — the first stage takes a variable number of 3D-printed Agnilet engines — and it flies from Agnikul's own 'Dhanush' launchpad.

faq.question: How much is Agnibaan designed to lift?
faq.answer: Up to about 300 kg to a 700 km low Earth orbit in its planned orbital configuration.

faq.question: Has Agnibaan reached orbit?
faq.answer: Not yet; the 2024 flight was a suborbital demonstrator and the orbital vehicle is in development.
